question: Which of the following constant values given in the options is equal to the universal gravitational constant 'G"?
solution:
The Correct answer is __**6.7 × 10⁻¹¹ Nm² kg⁻²**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **universal gravitational constant (G)** is a key constant in Newton's law of gravitation.
 
• Newton's law of gravitation states that the force of attraction between two masses is directly proportional to the product of their masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them.
 
• The value of **G** is **6.7 × 10⁻¹¹ Nm² kg⁻²**.
 
• This constant is crucial for calculations in **astrophysics and cosmology**, such as determining the gravitational force between celestial bodies.
 
• The unit of G, **Nm² kg⁻²**, helps in balancing the equation of gravitational force, ensuring that the force is measured in Newtons (N).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **9.8 ms⁻²**__

 __
 
• This value represents the **acceleration due to gravity (g)** on the surface of the Earth.
 
• It is the acceleration experienced by an object in free fall within a vacuum near the Earth's surface.
 
 
 
• **1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C**__
 __
 
• This value is the **elementary charge (e)**, which is the magnitude of the electric charge carried by a single proton or electron.
 
• It is a fundamental constant in physics and is crucial for calculations in electromagnetism and quantum mechanics.
 
 
 
• **9.1 × 10⁻³¹ kg**__
 
 
• This value represents the **mass of an electron**.
 
• The mass of an electron is significantly smaller than that of protons and neutrons, which are approximately 1.67 × 10⁻²⁷ kg.
